newsitem.title: FRANCE: Algeria courts jail bankers, pursue others.
newsitem.headline: Algeria courts jail bankers, pursue others.

text.p: Algerian courts said on Wednesday they had jailed around a dozen officials, including senior bank officers, for corruption. Some 40 more people faced similar trials.

In one of the toughest sentences, an official at the National Bank of Algeria (BNA) was sentenced by the court in the Saharan oasis town of Laghouat to 18 years imprisonment for embezzlement of public funds and for fraud.
In the northern port town of Skikda, the court sentenced the postmaster from nearby Azzaba to 20 years' jail for embezzlement.

A series of court announcements from around Algeria, carried on the official Algerian news agency APS, showed nearly a dozen other officials given terms in prison ranging from one year. Four accused were acquitted.
According to the court reports, around 40 more people including bank cashiers, a department head at the BNA bank in Oran, and watchmen were facing trial on similar charges.

In two townhalls, officials appointed by the government to run the local council from which Islamists had been expelled, also faced charges, ranging from corruption and abuse of influence to falsifying commercial documents and squandering public money.
In one instance, the local council leader faced charges with six local businessmen and two shopkeepers, while in the other he faced trial with 10 local businessmen.
Late last month, a court in Djelfa, 230 km (140 miles) south of Algiers condemned 22 people to death in absentia for embezzling assets of a state-owned enterprise.
